content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Use present simple affirmative for a short school-day routine. Model: “I get up at six and start class at eight.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use a school-day routine clearly and politely. One useful response is: “I get up at six and start class at eight.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where a school-day routine is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Join get up as two short beats; stress BREAKfast. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Join get up as two short beats; stress BREAKfast.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.

speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about a school-day routine.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using a school-day routine; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise a school-day routine?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: I get up at six and start class at eight.

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.

Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.

writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about a school-day routine. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: I get up at six and start class at eight. Submit your draft first.
